title: Basic Calculator
summary: Given a string s representing a valid mathematical expression, create a basic calculator to compute its value without using any built-in evaluation functions.
statement: Given a string s representing a valid mathematical expression, create a basic calculator to compute its value without using any built-in evaluation functions.
constraints: s is a valid 1–300000 character expression containing digits, spaces, +, -, and parentheses. Every number and running result fits signed 32-bit.
Unary minus is allowed, including before a parenthesized expression; unary plus and built-in expression evaluators are forbidden. Parentheses can be deeply nested.
hints: A sign applies to the number or complete parenthesized group that follows it.
Keep the current subtotal and sign; save both when entering a parenthesis.
On ')', finish the inner subtotal, multiply it by the saved sign, and add the saved outer subtotal.
Use an explicit stack rather than recursive evaluation so valid very deep parentheses do not hit Python's recursion limit.
editorial: Numbers are accumulated digit by digit. Plus or minus commits the preceding number and selects the next sign. An opening parenthesis saves the outer subtotal and sign; a closing parenthesis combines the completed inner value with that context. The independent oracle uses recursive descent on small generated expressions, while deterministic deep fixtures verify that the submitted approach must tolerate source-scale nesting.

tests.explanation: Adding the two operands gives 2; spaces do not affect the expression.
The inner group is 11, the first outer group is 9, and adding 14 gives 23.
